title: First-order logic
summary: First-order logic quantifies over objects while keeping predicates and functions in a fixed signature.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared formal logic context is fixed.

content.plain: First-order logic quantifies over objects while keeping predicates and functions in a fixed signature.
content.exact: An FOL presentation declares terms, formulas, variable binding, equality if used, a proof calculus, and Tarskian semantics for structures.
content.example: Group theory can be axiomatized in a first-order language with multiplication, identity, and inverse.
content.caveat: FOL is one highly successful framework, not the unique language of mathematics.
